page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-30 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor providing 30 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 15 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 120.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include per-core L1 data cache of 32 KB, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The instance includes no integrated local storage and no bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core computational capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2,862.37 placing in the top quartile. General multi-core compute metrics fall within the middle range, yielding a stress-ng multi-core score of 43,044.91, a Geekbench multi-core score of 14,302.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 41,531.46. Memory operations show mixed behavior: small-block cached read bandwidth reaches 2,124.87 GB/sec and the PassMark memory score is in the top 25% (2,761.2), yet uncached large-block write bandwidth drops to 25.49 GB/sec, ranking in the lower quartile.

For application runtimes, the c3d-standard-30 maintains balanced performance across web and data workloads. It delivers 21.89 GB/sec of static web serving throughput and handles 39.4 million Redis SET operations per second. LLM inference performance varies by model size: it achieves strong generation performance with small models (328.85 tokens/sec on 135M parameters), but drops to 7.43 tokens/sec on large 70B prompt processing due to the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators. Overall, the system provides consistent CPU and memory resources suited for enterprise web serving, backend application servers, mid-sized database systems, and CI/CD compilation pipelines reliant on external network-attached storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-30 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 30 vCPUs (15 physical cores) on an AMD EPYC 9B14 x86_64 processor and 120.0 GB of RAM. The instance features dedicated CPU execution with AVX-512 instruction support, 32 MB of L3 cache, no bundled local storage, and zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluation indicates upper-quartile single-core CPU compute and strong memory evaluation in PassMark, alongside balanced multi-core metrics, including 43,044.91 in stress-ng and 14,302.0 in Geekbench. Large uncached write bandwidth is a comparative bottleneck at 25.49 GB/sec, and high-parameter LLM tasks remain limited by lack of hardware acceleration. Operating at a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, it is suited for enterprise application hosting, relational databases, static web serving, and CI/CD compilation pipelines.
